# Slice 5 lifecycle evidence

Disposable real Git repositories contain an approved public product package, product source, Node-based package scripts and a pnpm lockfile. Private host config is absent until the separately approved manual application fixture. Synthetic reviewer/human receipts simulate workflow data; they do not prove live review, cryptographic identity or genuine consent.

Discovery and readiness helpers are invoked against unchanged host files, including absent/legacy config, supported facts and invalid proposals. Baseline fixtures invoke real pnpm scripts with automatic setup disabled; failures, stderr, tracked mutation after failure, unexpected output, ignored coverage, timeout and output overflow are observed. No baseline helper edits source, config or validation policy. A bounded prerequisite repair is performed explicitly by test code, committed as a separate host change and followed by rediscovery/reassessment.

Approved application and detachment are performed by fixture code outside the read-only helpers, simulating the human/orchestrator. File snapshots, default package validation, hook verification, routing/history preservation, append-only exclusions and removal preservation are checked. Shared host files remain. All original Slice 1–4 regressions run with `pnpm test:tophat`.

Fixtures test Windows/POSIX-shaped syntax and case collisions on Linux, not native Windows/macOS execution. They are not a live Antigravity interception demonstration. Node built-in type stripping does not type-check TypeScript. subprocess output buffers/timeouts are bounded, not process-tree memory or arbitrary script permissions.
